Polyclinic Hospital
This hospital, at 2601 North Third Street, for blocks north of the project, is the largest community hospital in Pennsylvania. The facility is a general community and treating hospital with 864 beds. It sustained heavy damage to equipment during the flood.
Hamilton Health Center
This facility is in the process of being established. When fully operational, it will provide personalized, comprehensive health care for the residents of the Hamilton NDP area; however, its services are not restricted to the Hamilton residents only. The services of the center may be expanded to include the project area. The center will be staffed with full-time medical and dental teams coordinated with health service programs of Federal, State and local agencies.
(3)Library Systems
The Harrisburg library system is composed of a main library and five branches. The main library is located near the project at Fourth and Walnut Streets. It has 110,000 volumes in the main library with approximately 30,000 volumes at the other locations. The system also operates a bookmobile that services the project area. The Pennsylvania State library with 500,000 volumes is also located within the City.
(4) Recreation
The City of Harrisburg has adopted standards established by the National Recreation and Park Association for its Recreational Programs. The facilities and parks supporting this program are composed of properties that vary in funcions, size, location and service. The parks are located throughout the City with one of the major parks being part of the project area--River Front Park (See Project Location Map, appendix B). River Front Park runs a distance of 40 blocks along Front Street, from Vaughn Street at the northern City Limits, south to Dock Street at the dam and Route I-83. This park was one of a series of municipal improvements which began with the first municipal loan of 1902. A walkway along the River, with steps leading down to it from Front Street, was constructed in large part between 1904 and 1912. The Park is noted for its beautiful flowers, particularly the Sunken Garden at Front and Verbeck Street. The Sunken Garden is within the project area. Use of River Front park is particularly high in the summer months by both project residents and visitors to the area. The Park is maintained by the City government, Department of Public Works.
